		<category name="BLassic Mode">
			<category name="Description">
				<comment>It's recommended to use this with a new character. It shouldn't delete anything on old characters, but certain weapon parts that wouldn't normally be on certain gun types in this pack may be there otherwise. Mostly grips. </comment>
				<comment>This mod is probably incompatible with 99% of weapon/shield/grenade replacers. Relic mods should be alright to use, and any class mod that doesn't have health regen should work fine.</comment>
				<comment>Don't try to use this with mod packs like Reborn. You're probably gonna have a bad time.</comment>
				<comment>For whatever reason, any hotfixes to a character's skill that added weapon swap speed like the UCP's Quicken or UCP With Claws crashed the game on certain menus, so those have been removed.</comment>
				<comment>The Buffed Loading Screen also sometimes crashed the game, so it has been removed.</comment>
				<category name="Gear">
					<category name="Weapons">
						<comment>Weapons are overhauled to be similar to what Borderlands 1 has. Barrels, Sights, Accessories, Stocks all replicate the respective parts from Borderlands 1.</comment>
						<comment>The bodies normally used for Common through Very Rare weapons now correspond to bodies 2 through 5 of Borderlands 1.</comment>
						<comment>Materials similarly correspond to the materials from Borderlands 1. BL1 Material 2 has been split between the Uncommon materials and Rare materials. Gemstone material is essentially a step above Material 3 from Borderlands 1.</comment>
						<comment>Grips now serve as the equivalent to Borderlands 1's magazines. Therefore, some grips shouldn't be on some weapon types, like how the Jakobs "Pounder" AR grip shouldn't spawn on Support Machineguns</comment>
						<comment>You can check the "Grips" categories in the various weapon types within "Specific Weapon Type Changes" to see what should spawn on what.</comment>
						<comment>Use Gibbed Save Editor to fix this if you plan on using this with a normal save file.</comment>
						<comment>The Gearbox gun bodies and the Starter gun barrel have been turned into Actions for non-revolver pistols.</comment>
						<comment>Additional accessories have been made to go along with Borderlands 1's accessories.</comment>
						<comment>Special weapons are converted and adjusted to fit Borderlands 1's scaling, with some getting buffed or nerfed depending on the item.</comment>
						<comment>Splash and Critical damage boosts have been adjusted on a case-to-case basis.</comment>
						<comment>Jakobs no longer fires as fast as you can pull the trigger.</comment>
						<comment>Normal Maliwan Pistols/Snipers and Torgue Pistols/Shotguns/Assault Rifles have less base damage but have 50% splash damage. They also fire projectiles at normal speed (no more Gyrojets for Torgue).</comment>
						<comment>Hyperion no longer has inverted recoil, Dahl no longer burst-fires while aiming down the sight (in most cases), Jakobs no longer fires as fast as you can pull the trigger (in most cases).</comment>
						<category name="Specific Weapon Type Changes">

								<comment>Jakobs, Maliwan, and Torgue are Revolvers.</comment>
								<comment>Bandit and Vladof are Machine Pistols.</comment>
								<comment>Repeaters and Machine Pistols can spawn with actions (which are converted from the gearbox weapon bodies and the starter pistol barrel).</comment>

					<category name="Shields">
						<comment>Shields are somewhere in between BL1 and BL2, largely due to BL2 having a lot more shield parts than BL1.</comment>
						<comment>The overall max capacity/delay/rate should be similar to BL1, depending on the parts.</comment>
						<comment>The ratio of stats boosted are similar to what they are in BL2, with special the same as before.</comment>
						<comment>Tediore shields have bonus recharge rate and delay, Pangolin shields have bonus capacity, and Anshin shields have passive health regeneration.</comment>
					</category>

					<category name="Rarity">
						<comment>There are three options for rarity, located at Borderlands Classic Mode > Gear > Rarity > Rarity Options.</comment>
						<comment>One that has everything have one color for each rarity except Legendary (which has multiple shades).</comment>
						<comment>Semi-Expanded option that has everything Legendary and beyond have multiple shades.</comment>
						<comment>Fully-Expanded option that gives all the rarities shades like Legendary has.</comment>
						<comment>Each of the above options also has an option to turn money into a minty color.</comment>
						<category name="Rarity Order">

				<category name="Drops">
					<comment>Drops are more generous compared to normal Borderlands 2. Legendaries, for example are a 1-in-500 chance instead of 1-in-10000 chance. Should match up fairly well with Borderlands 1's drops.</comment>
					<comment>Raid bosses now tend to drop a few world drop legendaries on a kill along with plenty of purples, similar to Crawmerax (Senior) but less excessive.</comment>
					<comment>Enemies drop whatever they're packing.</comment>
				</category>
				<category name="Elements">
					<comment>Elements work similar to how they are in Borderlands 1, minus the tech.</comment>
					<comment>Because of the lack of tech, they only have a 20% damage reduction compared to BL1's 40% damage reduction.</comment>
					<comment>Corroding an enemy makes them more vulnerable to damage.</comment>
					<comment>Slag works as it does in UVHM-RB in that it debuffs enemies.</comment>
				</category>
				<category name="Scaling">
					<comment>The game's scaling is pretty similar if not identical to Borderlands 1's scaling. Health, Shields, Damage, etc...</comment>
					<comment>At late game, damage numbers tend to lurk in the thousands range, instead of the hundred-thousands-to-millions-range.</comment>
				</category>
				<category name="Optionals">
					<category name="Parts with optional nerfs">
						<comment>Masher accessory (Consumes two ammo per shot)</comment>
						<comment>Double Anarchy (Consumes four ammo per shot)</comment>
						<comment>Five-Burst Rocket Launcher Barrel and Bunny (Damage reduction, on by default)</comment>
						<comment>Triple-Shot Rocket Launcher barrel and Roaster/Badaboom (Damage reduction, on by default)</comment>
					</category>
					<comment>Enemy non-weapon damage (Melee and basically anything that isn't an outright gun you could use) can seem lackluster on a decent amount of enemies (especially in the first few experience levels), so there's an option to improve it.</comment>
					<comment>The old quirk of being able to equip a weapon two levels above your own returns. It's on by default.</comment>
					<comment>The Crit can either have the chance to slip from your hands lowered or removed entirely.</comment>
					<comment>The Fabled Tortoise and Hoplite normally spawn with two bodies instead of one body anda  battery due to a mistake in the game's code. There's an option to remedy that, but it will delete the normal (bugged) Fabled Tortoises and Hoplites that you may have in a save that is loaded while the mod is active.</comment>
					<comment>BLassic is compatible with Koby's Level 1 UVHM. You'll need to hex-edit your game to enable level 1 UVHM, as well need to use Gibbed Save Editor to alter the Gearbox guns so they don't disappear.</comment>
					<comment>(Replace their unique Gearbox bodies with the gun body that is appropriate for the gun. Hyperion SMG body for the SMG, Vladof AR body for the Assault Rifle, Jakobs Sniper Rifle body for the sniper Rifle.)</comment>
					<comment>There is an option to allow Pearlescents, Ancient Relics, and legendary COMs to start dropping at level 1 instead of 50.</comment>
					<comment>There's an option to fiddle with the Sand Hawk so that it can no longer "Beehawk" effectively.</comment>
					<comment>There's an optional nerf to the Bee that drastically reduces the amp damage, but improves the capacity and delay of the shield.</comment>
					<comment>With how melee has been rigged, Zer0 would be doing absurd amounts of damage with a roid shield while in Decepti0n, even at the highest difficulty. Thus, a nerf to reduce roid damage by 75% (while in Decepti0n) is on by default, in "Recommended Nerfs".</comment>
					<comment>Similarly to Zer0, Krieg would be chunking out a bit too much damage with Roid, regardless of whether or not he is using his Action Skill. Due to a lack of better alternatives, I had to apply the Roid Damage nerf to his Class Mods, since I was unable to apply it directly to him. This nerf is in "Recommended Nerfs". If you're using one of my class mod packs, there's a seperate file that adjust those COMs to work with the roid nerfs (load that file after the COM mods.)</comment>
				</category>
